overall: The AG found the Subcommittee violated the Open Meeting Law by giving inadequate alternative public access to its virtual October 6 meeting and by holding an improper emergency meeting, and ordered minutes created and future compliance.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Oct 6 virtual meeting notice lacked enough location information to allow real-time public access.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Subcommittee failed to provide adequate alternative means of access to its October 6 meeting, and therefore, the meeting was not accessible to the public, in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Subcommittee held an improper emergency meeting on Oct 6, posted on short notice to meet a DESE budget report deadline.
allegations.key_passage: Because there was no valid emergency basis for this meeting, we find that the Subcommittee violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Not raised in the complaint; AG noted no minutes were made of the Oct 6 meeting and ordered minutes created to the best of the body's ability.
allegations.key_passage: We order the Subcommittee, if it has not already done so, to create minutes of the meeting held on October 6 to the best of its ability, through whatever means are available, including the memories and individual notations of the attendees.

remedy: Create minutes of the October 6 meeting to the best of the Subcommittee's ability, if not already done, using available means including attendees' memories and notes.
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements, with a caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
